chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih Al-Thawri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ordered Qanbar to whip a man with a Hadd (fixed punishment). Qanbar was harsh and increased by three lashes. So Ali (peace be upon him) caused retaliation from Qanbar for the three (excessive) lashes.

key_terms.حَدّاً: Hadd (a fixed punishment prescribed by Sharia)

ai.seo_question: How is Qisas applied to a servant who exceeds the limits of a judicial punishment?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the principle of proportional retaliation (Qisas) within the judicial authority of the Imam, demonstrating that Ali (peace be upon him) personally enforced the exact excess inflicted by his servant Qanbar. It highlights the precision required in administering Hadd punishments and serves as a practical example of justice being applied even to those in service, reinforcing the concept of accountability in Islamic jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih Al Sowry, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said that Amir Al-Momineenasws ordered Qanbar that he should whip a man, a Penalty (Hadd). So Qanbar was harsh, and increased by three lashes. So Aliasws caused retaliation from Qanbar of the three (excessive) lashes’.
